sentences.text:
The petitioner through the medium of present application is seeking regular bail in a case arising out of FIR No.65 of 2024 for offences under Sections 75 (i) (ii) (iii), 77, 78, 351(3) BNS 376,354B,
506 IPC, registered with Police Station, Charar-i-Sharief Budgam.

2. Learned counsel for the respondent has raised a preliminary objection to the maintainability of bail application before this Court on the ground that the petitioner has not exhausted his remedy before the Court of first instance and has directly filed bail application before this Court.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner had moved the Court of learned Sessions Judge, Budgam for grant of bail, but the same was withdrawn by him in terms of Order dated 14.09.2024 passed by the learned Sessions Judge and as such, it is not a case where the petitioner has not exhausted his remedy by filing bail application before the Court of first instance.
He has also submitted that in terms of Section 439 of Cr.P.C the Court of a Sessions Court and High Syed Arif Saleem Shah vs Union Territory Of J&K Through Police ... on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106727106/
1 Court have concurrent jurisdiction to entertain the bail application of an accused and, as such, the petitioner can directly approach this Court.

entities.label: COURT

entities.text: High Syed Arif Saleem Shah vs Union Territory Of J&K
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
5. There is no doubt to the legal position that Court of Sessions and High Court have concurrent jurisdiction to consider the bail application of an accused, but then this Court has in a number of judgments, including the one delivered in the case of Mohd Shafi Masi vs. UT of J&K and anr.,
passed in bail Application 13 of 2024 decided on 14.02.2024 laid down a rule practice that normally accused are required to first approach the Court of first instance instead of directly approaching the High Court.

entities.text: Mohd Shafi Masi vs. UT of J&K and anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is only in appropriate cases where the circumstances warrant so, that the High Court would entertain a bail application directly.
6. In the present case the petitioner has not spelled out any compelling or exceptional reasons that would show that his bail application should be directly entertained by this Court.

It is true that the petitioner had approached the learned Sessions Judge, Budgam, but it is also a fact that he has withdrawn the said bail application, meaning thereby that he has not exhausted the remedy that was available to him before the Court of first instance.
Without exhausting the remedy and getting adjudication of bail application on its merits by the Court of first instance, the petitioner could not have approached this Court directly.
7. It has been submitted by learned counsel for the respondents that during the pendency of this bail application the challan has been produced before the trial Court.

8. In view of what has been discussed hereinabove and having regard to the fact that challan stands already filed before the trial Court, it would be appropriate for the petitioner to approach the said Court for grant of bail in the first instance.

9 . For the foregoing reasons the application is held to be not maintainable and is, accordingly,
dismissed with leave and liberty to the petitioner to approach the trial Court.
